author: 𝕘𝕣𝕚𝕤𝕥
content: We were discussing/spitballing F2P models the other night. Just a few people. I’m sure as a community we can figure something out. The impetus is the move another project is making that is interesting. They will allow players to choose to opt out. So, imagine when Fortnite dropped you could go crypto or traditional. You buy some OG skins, grind out battle pass and all is good. Then a year later you “get it.” You see how much your OG skins are selling. But no worries. The project will then convert your account to crypto (they use matic) and you then will take true ownership of your assets. SA won’t work like this of course….I just think it would help if there was some form of F2P to onboard tradgamers who are skeptical of this space. But who knows, the project is fronted by a very popular streamer so we could have a sea change take place and soon this model (true ownership) will be the norm.

content:
@defiantwyvern I think the hot gameplay wallet is an interesting suggestion whether it's done through the lending mechanism or not. What comes to mind though is that to play we would probably need to "stake" our ships to the gameplay smart contracts be it in SCREAM or UE5. That means it would be in our interests to have our entire fleet at work, so to speak.

That being said it doesn't seem like that would limit our risk exposure in the end, especially if we would leave our ships on passive earnings, like starbase defense, and there would be no reason to withdraw the fleet from game unless looking to sell.

author: [AEP] WindSplitter1 [AEP]
content:
The Cryptosphere is very rich and diverse. Though there's a lot I don't understand about eco- and tokenomics, I like the foundations it brings us. Made the SA Metaverse possible.
Yet, because it brings all sorts of people, this includes the bad ones too, which are focused on matters outside adding to their respective communities.

We invested a lot in this one and it's not guaranteed we will succeed. Adding those hardships onto our own shoulders doesn't seem palatable, especially when its optional since we can upgrade to a more secure environment.

For that, reason, I'll relinquish whatever rewards the badges might bring in the future in favour of better security. Some might be able to take the hit and rebuy their assets back, but this might not be easy for whoever invested millions or, by contrast, lack that capacity to begin with.

Stay safe folks.

author: Oscar GF | Starke FinanceUstur
content: I think the vision of Star Atlas was always a ecosystem more than a game itself. There will be many stuff interacting with SA onchain data. UE5 client is just a graphical front end that will interact with that data and bring you very powerful posibilities. WebGL is another graphical front end with way less HW requirements and there will be probably different webs and even clients using the SA SDKs that interact with the same onchain data. Everything depends on the game mechanics implemented on each but the goal of the ecosystem is also to grow in economical activity. I also wonder how all of this would work together but I think it would be very limiting to only allow interact to this ecosystem through a UE5 based client with huge HW requirements

author: [AEP] WindSplitter1 [AEP]
content:
Given the metaversal applications the UE experience is to bring, it will attract all sorts of users (teachers, streamers, newscasters, etc...). I'd say users such as those @MrTixl said, would rather use the US platform (including those who are not yet part of the game, to tap into the SA community and expand their presence here, thus, contributing to our ecosystem. Likewise, this would create another much-needed ATLAS sink, for those who wish to charge a fee to access their content or donate to support the channel.

Furthermore, I'd suspect it is entirely possible for other companies (McDonald's, Adidas, Samsung, etc) to join as well and we can attend to their events or purchase their products directly from the game, which will further add to the UE version of the game.

As the vision of SCREAM is unlikely to serve anything other than the actual game, with some limitations due to its intended platform, I'd say that, despite its great potential, it will not attract as many players as the UE version: its intended target are players. Not streamers, etc.

author: [AEP] Bodhitree
content:
I have big respect for Axie. those of us that were preparing for months for ronin chain (eth gas free breeding) were some of the only ones to notice the bot farms scaling disproportionally. we were able to scale to hundreds of accounts (which is about how many one can scholar) with months of prep, and working full time. (I was even paying 30-50 scholars out of pocket from my irl job to scale faster untill i couldn't afford it anymore)

the bots themselves weren't all bad, they did create a lot of volume, and that pumped asset/axs prices, but it was purely extractive volume (despite axs breeding fee tax) and assets crashed harder than they did here.. it was bad they let allowed a game facet that could be botted to continue to rapidly scale for months unchecked. (it was a solid 2-3 months of 1 weeks roi) They made changes to limit bots compared to real players but it was many months too late. Lowering the returns would have worked (which would have made them less attractive as a project and that was their main value proposition at the time) or even understanding the bots could only do simple parts of the game and making changes to limit those facets of the game sooner would have helped. if they had made the changes sooner then scholars would have captured that value and for longer rather than giving bots the opportunity to scale untethered, and siphon value with overwhelming weight.
Another problem was they said we couldn't bot so that gave an even bigger advantage. @SW4GN3R finding a middle ground is exactly why i'm here, so thanks for that!

As long as bots are allowed for everyone to create competition, They cant outperform legit players again to create competition, and the roi is sustainable its all good

author: [AEP] Kavorka
content: Enabling any type of multi-period functionality within a single wallet would require significant restructuring of the codebase, as it is not supported within the Tribeca framework. It is something we are considering for the future. But to @[AEP] MoonMonger's point, with a new User Profile System in development, PVP would be aggregated across affiliated accounts.  In addition to this, and something we will be looking at implementing sooner, we will improve granularity of lock duration (right now minimum 1 year increments in those longer durations), such that you can select down the a daily interval, or simply select "Match Remaining Lock Duration"  Can't provide a time frame on those improvements, but the DAO team will be moving into upgrades/polish after ATLAS locking is implemented, as well as focusing on the Proposal and Voting system.

author: Oscar GF | Starke FinanceUstur
content: The biggest challenges in front of us are: 1. Building AAA games, generally, is a challenging undertaking (for any studio in pursuit of that level of quality) 2. Integrating blockchain into every element of Star Atlas. Utilizing NFTs, dual token native economy with governance, and on-chain logic  Of the two, blockchain is the true variable. We have experts across the team with demonstrated success in shipping AAA games, and the processes necessary to do so are documented. While every team might take a slightly different approach, there is historical data to work from. With respect to on-chain game development, we are absolute pioneers in this space, and no one is executing at a level we have envisioned. Therefore, it will require a lot of R&D, trial and error, and persistent iteration.  With that said, on-chain logic development does not slow down our AAA UE experience. Although we have already built a solana-native wallet integration into UE5 (first of its kind), for the most part, none of the on-chain logic is being delivered through UE at this time (although NFT integration is possible because of our wallet creation). The web-client will be the testbed for most of that logic, which is a strategic decision for multiple reasons. Primarily, we can build that client faster and integrate and iterate on the blockchain elements sooner. Our blockchain team is largely ahead of our game dev team for SCREAM (except for the instances in which certain logic isn't finalized, implying we can't actually build the on-chain program yet), so blockchain integration is not slowing down web-client development either.  ATMTA does not have any investors. The only audience we are accountable to is the community supporting us. We do have to strike balance between deliverables meeting community expectations, maintaining interest, and delivering what we believe to be the optimal product. However, our approach is to minimize scope and time-to-delivery, and maximize experience within those constraints. This is not a perfect science, and we continue to discuss that 'formula' internally, regularly. Over time, as more immersive experiences are released, it is likely that the time between major launches is extended, so we can fit more content into each release. Which should be acceptable, given there will be products the community can interact with.  If I were to add to the challenges, I would note that we are also quite literally building a studio from scratch at the same time we are pursuing some of the most innovative development the world has seen. While we have scaled successfully, coordinating 240 people in a fully remote environment, all whom have diverse backgrounds, requires a lot of internal work. And while the processes are executing well, they are constantly being refined. Our communication process is strong. But we can expect more efficiency out the team as we improve in that category as well.   And finally, I will add that in many cases, the technology we require to build simply does not exist (solana-UE5 wallet for example), so we have to build it just to facilitate the core game development. Which is why we have an entire division focusing on infrastructure development.

author: [AEP] Moustacheride
content: The biggest challenges in front of us are: 1. Building AAA games, generally, is a challenging undertaking (for any studio in pursuit of that level of quality) 2. Integrating blockchain into every element of Star Atlas. Utilizing NFTs, dual token native economy with governance, and on-chain logic  Of the two, blockchain is the true variable. We have experts across the team with demonstrated success in shipping AAA games, and the processes necessary to do so are documented. While every team might take a slightly different approach, there is historical data to work from. With respect to on-chain game development, we are absolute pioneers in this space, and no one is executing at a level we have envisioned. Therefore, it will require a lot of R&D, trial and error, and persistent iteration.  With that said, on-chain logic development does not slow down our AAA UE experience. Although we have already built a solana-native wallet integration into UE5 (first of its kind), for the most part, none of the on-chain logic is being delivered through UE at this time (although NFT integration is possible because of our wallet creation). The web-client will be the testbed for most of that logic, which is a strategic decision for multiple reasons. Primarily, we can build that client faster and integrate and iterate on the blockchain elements sooner. Our blockchain team is largely ahead of our game dev team for SCREAM (except for the instances in which certain logic isn't finalized, implying we can't actually build the on-chain program yet), so blockchain integration is not slowing down web-client development either.  ATMTA does not have any investors. The only audience we are accountable to is the community supporting us. We do have to strike balance between deliverables meeting community expectations, maintaining interest, and delivering what we believe to be the optimal product. However, our approach is to minimize scope and time-to-delivery, and maximize experience within those constraints. This is not a perfect science, and we continue to discuss that 'formula' internally, regularly. Over time, as more immersive experiences are released, it is likely that the time between major launches is extended, so we can fit more content into each release. Which should be acceptable, given there will be products the community can interact with.  If I were to add to the challenges, I would note that we are also quite literally building a studio from scratch at the same time we are pursuing some of the most innovative development the world has seen. While we have scaled successfully, coordinating 240 people in a fully remote environment, all whom have diverse backgrounds, requires a lot of internal work. And while the processes are executing well, they are constantly being refined. Our communication process is strong. But we can expect more efficiency out the team as we improve in that category as well.   And finally, I will add that in many cases, the technology we require to build simply does not exist (solana-UE5 wallet for example), so we have to build it just to facilitate the core game development. Which is why we have an entire division focusing on infrastructure development.

author: [AEP] Mandalorian (Djin Djarin)
content: The biggest challenges in front of us are: 1. Building AAA games, generally, is a challenging undertaking (for any studio in pursuit of that level of quality) 2. Integrating blockchain into every element of Star Atlas. Utilizing NFTs, dual token native economy with governance, and on-chain logic  Of the two, blockchain is the true variable. We have experts across the team with demonstrated success in shipping AAA games, and the processes necessary to do so are documented. While every team might take a slightly different approach, there is historical data to work from. With respect to on-chain game development, we are absolute pioneers in this space, and no one is executing at a level we have envisioned. Therefore, it will require a lot of R&D, trial and error, and persistent iteration.  With that said, on-chain logic development does not slow down our AAA UE experience. Although we have already built a solana-native wallet integration into UE5 (first of its kind), for the most part, none of the on-chain logic is being delivered through UE at this time (although NFT integration is possible because of our wallet creation). The web-client will be the testbed for most of that logic, which is a strategic decision for multiple reasons. Primarily, we can build that client faster and integrate and iterate on the blockchain elements sooner. Our blockchain team is largely ahead of our game dev team for SCREAM (except for the instances in which certain logic isn't finalized, implying we can't actually build the on-chain program yet), so blockchain integration is not slowing down web-client development either.  ATMTA does not have any investors. The only audience we are accountable to is the community supporting us. We do have to strike balance between deliverables meeting community expectations, maintaining interest, and delivering what we believe to be the optimal product. However, our approach is to minimize scope and time-to-delivery, and maximize experience within those constraints. This is not a perfect science, and we continue to discuss that 'formula' internally, regularly. Over time, as more immersive experiences are released, it is likely that the time between major launches is extended, so we can fit more content into each release. Which should be acceptable, given there will be products the community can interact with.  If I were to add to the challenges, I would note that we are also quite literally building a studio from scratch at the same time we are pursuing some of the most innovative development the world has seen. While we have scaled successfully, coordinating 240 people in a fully remote environment, all whom have diverse backgrounds, requires a lot of internal work. And while the processes are executing well, they are constantly being refined. Our communication process is strong. But we can expect more efficiency out the team as we improve in that category as well.   And finally, I will add that in many cases, the technology we require to build simply does not exist (solana-UE5 wallet for example), so we have to build it just to facilitate the core game development. Which is why we have an entire division focusing on infrastructure development.

author: DRUMCARL05 | ⭐Polaris Fuel⛽MUD
content:
My 2 cents based in several conversations about fees since the bomb was dropped: 

I think that 6% fee is incentive enough for large organizations of players (the people) in the business of producing refined resources and parts, specially taking into account that you may be paying that fee several times in your line of production indefinitely. 

The alternative of staking $40,000 in Atlas to reduce fees in less than half is pretty much non existent, considering it’s an inflationary token (not ideal for large amounts of staking). The last tier of discount I won’t even comment ($600,000!!!!!). 

I can think of several business minded player organizations ⛽️ that are already looking for the tools needed to conduct these trades outside of the marketplace for these reasons. Geolocation becomes less important if you are already organized in game and materials are just changing hands outside the marketplace, but the operation is happening within your same faction/area. 

If there was another way to achieve this level of fee reduction other than staking an insane amount of Atlas through game mechanics for the average hard working player/organization, then for sure the marketplace would be the way to go. 

For a few of us, the top Atlas staking tiers seem the typical pay to win advantages only available for big whales or big business (the man). 

Once you have final products, then it makes more sense to sell to the wide population of players in the marketplace and pay your fee and contribute to both development and DAO.
Maybe this approach is due to lack of details regarding the distribution, and with the current dynamics where we are already contributing 100% on ships and resources directly to ATMTA. Many things will change in the coming years but right now the fee feels a little too much as a regular part of all multiplayer interactions/trades in every step of the production line. 

I hope I make sense and this is taken as constructive feedback. After all, we only have a screen shot to analyze.

author: [HEIM] SDU pimpUstur
content: The fact of the matter is that the average gamer is not going to care to close the game down, and look for what is basically a feeless p2p trade for the seller. Buyers will always look at the default marketplace first, as that will be the most accessible, and seeing as buyers are not paying fees (which they shouldn't), that is probably all the incentive needed to just post on the default marketplace. as for the fee, at the end of the day, it's all about just calculating what you want for the item, and if the fee is cutting into that, just hike up the price abit. Now of course, base items will be harder to do that, as alot of people will be competing against each other driving the price down, but just find a niche, and you won't even notice the fee. I have noticed fees generally in MMOs tend to be much higher than 6%, I think that fee is very reasonable, and people trying to skirt around it are basically just doing a in-person trade, which most MMOs offer anyway. I don't think it is game breaking, and I don't think that worrying about 100% of players using this feeless mechanism is something to worry about.

I don't think it is game breaking, and I don't think that worrying about 100% of players using this feeless mechanism is something to worry about.

author: DRUMCARL05 | ⭐Polaris Fuel⛽MUD
content:
Message for my fellow gamers as I already said my two cents to the SA team (which I love and respect and I’ll be here until the end no matter what). 

This is a healthy conversation to have in my opinion. We are not trying to change anyone’s minds or attack Star Atlas. We are just giving honest feedback. 

The whole concept of staking large amounts of money in an inflationary token to get a manageable discount on fees that are part most multiplayer interaction is challenging for many of us planing small and medium operations. Most of the answers are 100% speculative as we don’t know the volume of money we will handle and the DAO doesn’t have any tools yet. 6% seems an ok fee when you are buying resources for your fleet, but $6000 in fees hurt when you are selling a capital ship and take a huge slice of your gains when you are a ship trader (compared to our trading experience so far). 
Furthermore, large mining operations will incur in fees several times on the chain and whales will have a huge advantage in gains just for being in a different tax bracket. Multi-sig treasury wallets require several people to approve transactions and take away all critical timing responses to the market, adding all kind of levels of complexity. No one is accusing the Star Atlas team of any wrong doing with their profit (we trust them 100%), but for several years to come we won’t have an immersive experience where these fees are the only income, so it shouldn’t be too hard to understand that some of us are concerned, as these news impact heavily our business plans. Maybe 72,000,000 Atlas will be an average amount to have for any organization. It won’t be the case for several years and no one can predict when these levels of volume will become a thing. Maybe DAO tools that simplify the process to manage thousands of members assets and operations to interact with the marketplace will be developed and available to us soon. 
If you are ok paying 6% or 10% that’s great. I imagine just based on security and ease of use alone most regular players will be ok with this fee. Other games have charged way more for stuff you don’t even own. We get that. 
But this is not Amazon or Facebook, it’s a decentralized prospect project that we are all helping to build. 
So please don’t feel like we are attacking the project, we are not. We care, and we are just expressing our point of view with this amazing opportunity we have to speak directly with the people that matters. We are extremely lucky to have this opportunity and this won’t last forever, as numbers will explode with new players some day (probably soon!). 

I still see a parallel market as my only option for the time being with the current situation and information available to be able to set a competitive enterprise. Seeing what we have seen from the beginning with the talent in this community, it won’t take us long to develop solutions that will adapt to all our game styles (god bless decentralization and crypto). I can’t wait to work out all the challenges and opportunities we will have in the years to come. So cheers and have a great weekend

author: SW4GN3R [STAR]
content:
Lot of discourse in here overnight regarding marketplace fees and associated discounts. I think perhaps it helps to emphasize two points:
1. ATLAS locked benefits every single user in the ecosystem, not just the person performing the lock. This can be associated with available inventory and velocity of money, both of which are reduced with locked balances. So while someone locking 72M ATLAS will be the beneficiary of the marketplace discount, all gamers, players, marketplace traders, etc. will see benefits. Don't forget, your earnings are all denominated in ATLAS, so any tokenomic element benefitting that currency directly benefits you.

2. We went through an extensive analysis on web3 fee structures, and models for fee discounts existing in crypto. What we arrived at, IMO, is a balanced combination of those existing models. The fee is far below web2 fees, and in-line with web3 fees. And as time progresses with crafting, and with many resources, components, items being collected as loot, earned not by spending but by playing, your cost basis is reduced to zero, with the exception of the time put into the game.

I'll add that I believe the POLIS rewards to not only be incentivizing, but elegantly crafted to encourage participation in the DAO, which unlocks governance features, additional POLIS rewards, and treasury management.

author: SW4GN3R [STAR]
content:
We want to fully support UGC - User Generated Content. I can't speak to the timing of that functionality, but it will likely be quite some time into the future. But I will suggest that the introduction of UGC is also going to be a slow, iterative process. author: ! ᚺEIM | VɪᴋɪɴɢᴇɴBᴇɴɴʏViking
content: Lot of discourse in here overnight regarding marketplace fees and associated discounts. I think perhaps it helps to emphasize two points: 1. ATLAS locked benefits every single user in the ecosystem, not just the person performing the lock. This can be associated with available inventory and velocity of money, both of which are reduced with locked balances. So while someone locking 72M ATLAS will be the beneficiary of the marketplace discount, all gamers, players, marketplace traders, etc. will see benefits. Don't forget, your earnings are all denominated in ATLAS, so any tokenomic element benefitting that currency directly benefits you.  2. We went through an extensive analysis on web3 fee structures, and models for fee discounts existing in crypto. What we arrived at, IMO, is a balanced combination of those existing models. The fee is far below web2 fees, and in-line with web3 fees. And as time progresses with crafting, and with many resources, components, items being collected as loot, earned not by spending but by playing, your cost basis is reduced to zero, with the exception of the time put into the game.  I'll add that I believe the POLIS rewards to not only be incentivizing, but elegantly crafted to encourage participation in the DAO, which unlocks governance features, additional POLIS rewards, and treasury management.

author: Kr1gs
content: I am not an econ expert, but generally if a currency is inflationary, there should be sinks (burn mechanisms) in place to counter that, it's a balance of sorts, a yin and yang. The reason this is done instead of just making something deflationary, is because inflationary is more dynamic, so it can support growth. Now ATLAS staking is not a sink per se, but it can perform a similar function in that a large amount of ATLAS will be locked and not in circulation. But what you said is correct, in that this won't necessarily make the token price go up, because at the end of the day ATLAS price is determined by the people that use it as a means of exchange, but it can help.

Here’s something I’ve been wondering about more frequently as we get closer to scream…

To what extent has the Econ team considered VWAP when determining game mechanics? i.e. if a ship has a VWAP of $10,000 how much effort/time is it going to take for a player using that ship to generate $10,000 worth of value? If it’s going to take 10 years of playing 8 hours per day with a moderately tuned min/max strat, no one is going to buy the ship for anywhere near VWAP, so we have permanent “discounts” and VWAP means nothing. If it’s ships generate more in SCORE than in SCREAM, then ship prices continue to go down, right?

content: Something I cannot imagine that they're going to balance is how every place is going to feel like it has a story and how there are going to be enough places. author: [AEP] Moustacheride
content: @Deleted User it’s hard to answer or provide input without know anything about the combat mechanics. Reason I asked the question is it came up in our internal discussions. If combat is deterministic and combat power is added to a starbase there needs to be a mechanic that the offensive side can party together fleets. If that is not an option perhaps they stay separate and can be manually targeted.

author: [AEP] Moustacheride
content: Also the in proximity of a starbase would perhaps provide some strategy in positioning that the other version does not but if the in proximity is harder to develop it makes sense not to have it.

author: [AEP] Moustacheride
content: Having ship fleets be individually targetable allows both large and small ships to contribute equally. Small ships can target small ship fleets. Larger ships can optimize larger targets.

author: [AEP] Moustacheride
content: If fleets are lumped together depending on how combat and damage is dished out it will disproportionately affect larger or smaller ships

author: [AEP] Moustacheride

Like if I’m defending a starbase with a tree arrow and all attacking fleet damage hits me first before the smaller ships that is adverse to having large ships.

As far as lp distribution it probably should go off of damage dealt and received

author: [EMP] jith blade
content: I think 24 hours is too long but I will say on the other hand the choice between locked cache and burning would be interesting to investigate. In many games once you reach certain levels somethings aren’t worth it for you to loot or coordinate a retrieval from someone who would actually want the resources. So you could either decide to have it be cached or burned so it doesn’t have to be dealt with. I would suggest to combat people just going around destroying and creating infinite locked caches all over space there could be use for the data runner or the scavenger ships to the affect that they might be able to hack or just break down the cache in terms of mini game play. It incentives actually coming back to them swiftly and efficiently from the attackers again keeping people from squirreling away loot boxes. Maybe fighters can shoot the boxes till the bust open but that is also even more inefficient since it burns even more of the loot inside for the brute force attack. You could also probably have people set up trades for loot boxes the old Amazon warehouse return mystery box resell trick you might be an attacker but like direct cash more so you can sell location and add them to the cache which I assume is temp escrow wallet so that way they can easily remove the contents since they paid for them directly en mass.

author: CheckmateONI
content:
chipping in my two atlas for the discussion:

players that had inventory within the starbase should absolutely forfeit that to the aggressors. dont store large amount of resources in a contested star base, put valuable ressources into CSS for "cold storage". incentivizes attacking SB's as the reward is LP + stored enemy SB inventory + battle loot.

when all three factions are present at a large starbase battle, nobody gets ownership of the SB upon destruction. the SB will simply be destroyed, and replaced by an empty "placeholder/ghost" of a starbase. one of those three factions could then re-initialize the starbase by paying a certain amount of ressources to begin the process of building the new starbase up from scratch (process takes time) while simultaneously defending it until completion. this phase will be very contested as the newly begun SB has low HP (like 20%) after re-initializing, thus can be destroyed quickly. there should be a cooldown per faction. if your faction attempted to build up the SB but it failed, the faction has to wait x period until it can make another attempt, gives the other two factions the opportunity to give it a try. the stronger fleet will likely be able to control/defend/build up the new SB, while minor factions retreat.
